Tiago Pereira (born 16 July 1980, in Lisbon, Portugal) is a retired Portuguese track and field athlete who specialized in the **3000 metres steeplechase**. Here's a comprehensive overview of his career and key details:

### 🏃‍♂️ Career Highlights & Achievements
- **Olympic Games**:  
  - Competed in **three consecutive Olympics**: Sydney 2000, Athens 2004, and Beijing 2008.  
  - His best Olympic finish was **7th place in the 3000m steeplechase at Athens 2004**, with a time of **8:14.84** — a then-Portuguese national record (later broken).  
  - Did not advance beyond the heats in Sydney (2000) or Beijing (2008).

- **World Championships**:  
  - Participated in four World Championships (1999, 2001, 2003, 2007), reaching the final only once — **5th place in Paris 2003**, finishing in **8:12.13**, his personal best and **long-standing Portuguese national record** (stood for 12 years until broken by Pedro Figueiredo in 2015).  
  - Was a consistent finalist at European level.

- **European Championships**:  
  - Won **bronze in Munich 2002**, finishing in **8:19.70**, Portugal’s first-ever European steeplechase medal.  
  - Also competed in 2006 (Gothenburg) and 2010 (Barcelona), reaching the final in 2006 (7th place).  
  - Was a three-time European Championships finalist.

- **European Indoor Championships**:  
  - Won **silver in Vienna 2002** in the 3000m (not steeplechase — an uncommon indoor distance for him), clocking **7:47.25**, showcasing his versatility.

- **Lusophone Games & Other Events**:  
  - Gold medalist at the 2006 Lusophone Games in Macau (3000m steeplechase).  
  - Multiple Portuguese national titles (11 national outdoor steeplechase titles between 1999–2011; also won national 5000m and cross country titles).

### 📈 Key Stats & Records
- **Personal Best**:  
  - **3000m steeplechase**: **8:12.13** (Paris, 2003) — former national record  
  - **3000m (indoor)**: 7:47.25 (Vienna, 2002)  
  - **5000m (outdoor)**: 13:31.37 (2003)  
- **National Records**:  
  - Held the Portuguese steeplechase record from 2003 to 2015.  
  - Also held national indoor 3000m record briefly.

### 🏅 Honors & Recognition
- Named **Portuguese Athlete of the Year** in **2003**, following his world championship 5th place and European success.  
- Recipient of the **Grand Cross of the Order of Merit** (Grã-Cruz da Ordem do Mérito) in 2004 — one of Portugal’s highest civilian honors — awarded for sporting excellence and contribution to national pride.  
- Inducted into the **Portuguese Sports Hall of Fame** (Casa do Desporto Português) in 2015.

### 🧭 Background & Training
- Trained under renowned coach **José Peseiro** early on, later working extensively with Spanish coach **José Luis Mendoza**, who also coached Alberto García and other elite Spanish distance runners.  
- Represented the clubs **Clube Oriental de Lisboa**, **Sporting CP**, and **S.L. Benfica** during his career.  
- Known for his tactical intelligence, endurance, and strong finishing kick — excelling particularly in championship-style racing.

### 🎓 Education & Post-Athletics Life
- Holds a degree in **Sports Sciences** from the Technical University of Lisbon (now part of Universidade de Lisboa).  
- After retiring from athletics in **2012**, he transitioned into coaching and sports administration:  
  - Served as **Technical Director of Athletics at the Portuguese Olympic Committee** (2013–2017).  
  - Worked as a **coach and mentor** for emerging Portuguese distance runners, including at Benfica’s youth academy.  
  - Occasionally contributes as a sports commentator and analyst for RTP (Rádio e Televisão de Portugal) during major athletics events.  
  - Involved in anti-doping education and youth sports development initiatives in Portugal.

### 🧩 Personal & Legacy
- Known for his humility, professionalism, and strong advocacy for clean sport and athlete welfare.  
- Considered a **pioneer and benchmark for Portuguese steeplechase running**, paving the way for successors like Ivo Oliveira (who later excelled in 1500m) and more recently, steeplechase talents like João Coelho and José Marques.  
- His 2002 European bronze remains one of only two individual European track & field medals for Portugal in men’s distance events (alongside Alberto Paulo’s 2006 3000m steeplechase silver — though Pereira’s was earlier and in a deeper field).

### 📚 Additional Notes
- Never tested positive for doping; consistently passed all WADA and national anti-doping controls.  
- Appeared in several Portuguese documentaries on Olympic history and national sporting legacy (e.g., *Ouro na Pista*, RTP, 2012).  
- Has spoken publicly about the challenges of sustaining elite endurance careers in smaller athletics nations — advocating for improved infrastructure, funding, and scientific support in Portuguese athletics.

Tiago Pereira is widely regarded as **one of Portugal’s greatest middle- and long-distance runners of the 2000s**, and a defining figure in the modern history of Portuguese athletics.
